akane.peak: Early season (NFC picks mid August); Orange Pippin says it does not keep well, best eaten fresh
akane.notes: No source mentions the strong perfume behind our 'perfumed' tag.

anna.peak: Very early (June); keeps about a week (Orange Pippin)
anna.notes: English Wikipedia page has no flavour words. Nothing found for our 'floral' or 'herbal' tags.

ariane.peak: Best served slightly chilled (Orange Pippin); Wikipedia says it keeps three months or more and is good refrigerated for winter eating
ariane.notes: French Wikipedia (same organisation, not counted separately) calls it 'croquante, juteuse, acide et sucrée'. No source found for 'perfumed'.

autumn-pearmain.peak: Mid-September in Salt Spring's orchard; picked late September at NFC
autumn-pearmain.notes: Orange Pippin slug redirects to home page; no English Wikipedia page. NFC says its trees are indistinguishable from Herefordshire Pearmain. Salt Spring Apple Company is an orchard/nursery and cidery.

battleford.peak: Late Aug-early Sep; stores about 4 weeks (USask compilation)
battleford.notes: USask sheet compiles several prairie references (Leslie 1946, Nelson 1976, Peters, Stushnoff 1985); counted as one source. Prairie Gardens wording may derive from the same prairie literature.

ben-davis.peak: Winter keeper (Orange Pippin); about 5 months refrigerated (Salt Spring)
ben-davis.notes: Orange Pippin text says 'not particularly flavorful' while its multi-valued attribute list includes Sweet/Sharp, Sweeter and Aromatic; the 'perfumed' tag rests only on that attribute and conflicts with the text. NFC description is of a coloured sport of Ben Davis received from Yugoslavia. English Wikipedia has no flavour words. All three agree on little flavour; Salt Spring uses 'mild'.

binet-rouge.peak: Picked late November (Orange Pippin); mid-October on Salt Spring Island; can take some sweating before pressing
binet-rouge.notes: No en/fr Wikipedia page; not in NFC search.

bortlinger-weinapfel.peak: Picking ripe mid October, processed through November (de.wikipedia)
bortlinger-weinapfel.notes: Not on Orange Pippin or NFC.

bramleys-seedling.peak: Cooking apple; Scott Farm harvests mid-September into October
bramleys-seedling.notes: Orange Pippin page is at slug 'bramley' (bramleys-seedling redirects to home). Scott Farm is an orchard, recorded as nursery.

calville-daout.notes: Not on Orange Pippin (not tried by slug), Wikipedia or NFC search.

centennial.peak: Mid to late August (UMN); does not store well; keeps 2-3 weeks (Orange Pippin)
centennial.notes: Orange Pippin page is under crab-apples (centennial-crab). Fedco says 'not sweet', which conflicts with our sweet 3 and summary 'sweet-sharp'; a web-search snippet elsewhere called the flesh 'sweet, and mildly acidic' but that page was not fetched.

cornish-gilliflower.storage_change: Flavour and smell become more floral in storage (Scott Farm); keeps well into the new year (Orange Pippin)
cornish-gilliflower.peak: Can be eaten well into the new year (Orange Pippin)
cornish-gilliflower.notes: Orange Pippin's clove-like scent refers to the blossom. Wikipedia only gives the name etymology (girofle, clove) as a reference to its odour when cut. Nothing found for 'honey'.

coxs-pomona.notes: Orange Pippin slug coxs-pomona redirects to home page; no Wikipedia page found. NFC calls the flesh soft and sweet-subacid, Salt Spring calls it crisp and tart fresh (sweet only when cooked).

crispin.peak: Keeps 3 months or more (Orange Pippin); keeps up to three months (Wikipedia)
crispin.notes: Orange Pippin page is titled Mutsu. No source found for 'floral'. Trees of Antiquity (not counted, fetched later) calls the flesh 'slightly aromatic'; Chris Bowers says 'very, very pleasant'.

democrat.peak: Picked late October; keeps very long (NFC: over twelve months in Australia; Salt Spring: up to 7 months refrigerated)
democrat.notes: NFC 'Democrat (2)' (id 1536) is a different, American variety. Not on Orange Pippin or English Wikipedia.

duchess-of-oldenburg.peak: Harvested early-mid August; Scott Farm keeps them in cooler through September; Trees of Antiquity says storage 2-3 weeks
duchess-of-oldenburg.notes: NFC calls it only subacid, milder than our acid 5. Two nurseries call it (highly) aromatic, which our tags lack. English Wikipedia has no flavour words (purée with an orange tint).

early-harvest.peak: Eat fully ripe; also for sauce (Orange Pippin)
early-harvest.notes: Both call it 'subacid' (mildly acid), weaker than our 'sharp'/acid 4. Both descriptions look derived from the same old American description (NFC record is for a variety not held), so independence is doubtful.

envy.notes: Orange Pippin slug 'envy' redirects to home page; not in NFC search. Wikipedia says it keeps its firmness in storage and cut flesh browns very slowly.

flanders-cox.notes: No Orange Pippin, Wikipedia or NFC record found under this name.

frequin-rouge.peak: Early October on Salt Spring Island; press within a few weeks
frequin-rouge.notes: Orange Pippin is internally inconsistent: its text says 'bittersharp' while its juice-style attribute says 'Bittersweet (cider)'; Salt Spring says bittersweet. No en/fr Wikipedia page; not in NFC search.

gennet-moyle.peak: Picked late September (NFC); good for baking and drying
gennet-moyle.notes: NFC also holds 'Gennet Moyle (of Taylor)' (id 2413), a culinary/cider apple giving a light cider; same source, not counted twice. Not on Orange Pippin or Wikipedia.

golden-delicious.storage_change: Fruit picked green and stored for months (supermarket fruit) loses flavour; the true flavour shows only when ripened golden-green on the tree (Orange Pippin, Trees of Antiquity, Chris Bowers)

climate_flavour.note: Chris Bowers: needs higher temperature and light intensity, not successful everywhere in the UK; Orange Pippin: grows well in the UK given a warm, sheltered microclimate

golden-delicious.peak: Ripened on the tree to golden-green; picked early to late October
golden-delicious.notes: No source supports our 'honey' or 'pear-drop' tags.

goldrush.storage_change: Some sharpness at picking that mellows in storage (Orange Pippin, Trees of Antiquity); keeps 3 months or more, 6 months in a domestic fridge (Orange Pippin)
goldrush.peak: Picked very late (mid November); best after some storage
goldrush.notes: No English Wikipedia page (GoldRush and Goldrush_(apple) 404). Cummins id 3166 resolved to its GoldRush product page.

climate_flavour.note: Trees of Antiquity: best grown in warmer climates (growing advice; flavour not stated explicitly)

grimes-golden.peak: Harvest late September to mid October; keeps 1-3 months
grimes-golden.notes: Spice is supported by four sources. No modern source found for our 'pear' tag. Scott Farm adds banana and licorice.

harry-masters-jersey.notes: NFC page has no flavour text. Walcot notes the alias 'Port Wine'. No English Wikipedia page.

holstein.peak: Picked late September; eating ripe from October, stores to December or longer (de.wikipedia); Trees of Antiquity says 5-6 months refrigerated
holstein.notes: Perfumed/aromatic supported by four sources; pineapple only by Orange Pippin; spice by German Wikipedia. Chris Bowers also says 'highly aromatic'. English Wikipedia page does not exist.

climate_flavour.note: de.wikipedia: suited mainly to not-too-warm, rather moist sites (site advice)

ingrid-marie.peak: Ripe mid to late September, stores to about January (de.wikipedia); Orange Pippin says best straight from the tree
ingrid-marie.notes: Orange Pippin calls it bland and light, while Scott Farm and Trees of Antiquity call it (lightly) aromatic. English Wikipedia has no flavour words.

jonagold.peak: Picked early to mid October; keeps 1-2 months (Orange Pippin)
jonagold.notes: No source supports our 'honey' or 'pear-drop' tags. Chris Bowers (not counted) says 'superb flavour', 'richly flavoured'.

katy.storage_change: Refreshing straight from the tree but goes soft after a while; best kept in the fridge and eaten cool (Orange Pippin)

climate_flavour.note: Orange Pippin: one of the best for northern areas with short seasons, ripens even in a poor summer

katy.peak: Late August-early September for a few weeks; stores until October (Walcot)
katy.notes: Strawberry only from Orange Pippin. English Wikipedia has no flavour words.

kidds-orange-red.peak: Best before the New Year (Orange Pippin); Chris Bowers says November-December; Walcot stores until January
kidds-orange-red.notes: Aromatic is unanimous; honey and wine come only from Orange Pippin. Trees of Antiquity adds a hint of violets and says it performs well in hot interior climates. Walcot ('very good flavour') and Chris Bowers ('aromatic flavour', Cox-like) also fetched.

lady-northcliffe.notes: NFC holds an accession ('Lady Northcliffe' LA 74A, id 26) but the page has no description. Not on Orange Pippin; a web search found nothing.

laxtons-superb.peak: Picked early October; stores until January (Walcot); keeps 1-2 months (Orange Pippin)
laxtons-superb.notes: Texture disagreement: Orange Pippin says firm and not very juicy, NFC 'very juicy', Walcot 'crisp, juicy'. Salt Spring Apple Company (also fetched) says sweet with some complexity.

lobo.peak: Mid-September to November (La Pomme du Quebec); picked mid September (NFC)
lobo.notes: Orange Pippin page exists but has no flavour words ('McIntosh-style'). No English Wikipedia page. NFC 'rather soft' vs Quebec growers' 'crunchy'. La Pomme du Quebec is the Quebec apple producers' body.

lord-lambourne.peak: Picked mid to late September; stores until November (Walcot), 2 months refrigerated (Salt Spring)
lord-lambourne.notes: Sharpness is supported by three sources though our tags lack 'sharp'. Salt Spring adds strawberry (from the Worcester parent).

malus-sieversii.notes: English Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malus_sieversii) has no flavour words, only that crispness, flavour intensity and fruit weight were selected by humans. Not on Orange Pippin or NFC.

mere-de-menage.peak: Early October; keeps 3-4 months refrigerated (Salt Spring)
mere-de-menage.notes: Orange Pippin slug redirects to home page.

monidel.peak: Early to mid September; keeps 2-3 weeks (Orange Pippin) or up to 3 months refrigerated (Salt Spring)
monidel.notes: Both pages describe Delbarestivale (Estivale); Orange Pippin lists Monidel as one of its marketing names. No source found under the Monidel name itself. Neither mentions 'aromatic'.

norfolk-beefing.storage_change: Sharp at first, sweetens steadily in store and by March is sweet enough for dessert use; flesh grows harder and darker with keeping (Wikipedia, Chris Bowers)
norfolk-beefing.peak: Cook from early October; raw from about March
norfolk-beefing.notes: NFC is internally inconsistent: description 'very acid', characterisation 'subacid'. Orange Pippin page exists but has no flavour words. Chris Bowers says baked it develops a rich flavour and seldom needs sugar.

opalescent.peak: Harvest from mid-September; stores about 3 months and hangs well on the tree (Trees of Antiquity)
opalescent.notes: Orange Pippin page has no description text. Strawberry is reported by two nurseries but is not among our tags. Scott Farm's lilac is hedged ('some say'). No source uses 'perfumed'/'aromatic'.

parkland.peak: Mid to late August; USask compilation says it keeps 6-8 weeks
parkland.notes: Our 'mild' tag is not supported by either source; both stress tartness ('plain' in Orange Pippin is closest to mild). USask storage of 6-8 weeks contradicts our 'keeps poorly'.

pink-pearl.peak: Late August to mid-September; does not keep long on the tree or in store
pink-pearl.notes: No source supports our 'citrus' or 'lemon' tags. Wikipedia and Trees of Antiquity share the phrase 'tart to sweet-tart', so they may not be independent. Trees of Antiquity says the tartness depends on harvest time.

pomme-gris.peak: Very late (early November); keeps 2-3 months refrigerated (Salt Spring)
pomme-gris.notes: NFC record (Pomme Grise, not held) is a characterisation, probably from an old description. Nutty only from Salt Spring; no source says 'sweet' explicitly. Orange Pippin slugs pomme-gris/pomme-grise redirect to home page.

queen-cox.notes: No source supports our 'floral', 'pear-drop', 'honey' or 'rose' tags; they look borrowed from Cox descriptions. Orange Pippin slug redirects to home page; no Wikipedia page.

red-falstaff.peak: Picked late September-October; stores until January or longer (Chris Bowers), until March (Walcot), 1-2 months (Orange Pippin)
red-falstaff.notes: Flavour descriptions are generic; sharp rests only on Orange Pippin's style attribute.

reinette-clochard.peak: Picked mid to late October; keeps 3 months or more (Orange Pippin)
reinette-clochard.notes: Perfumed/aromatic is supported by NFC and Scott Farm but is not among our tags.

rosa-mantovana.notes: NFC record is under 'Rosa del Caldaro'. German Wikipedia's flavour sentence quotes Engelbrecht (19th century), so it overlaps with the book team. 'rosenapfelartig' refers to the Rosenapfel group, not a rose flavour. Orange Pippin slug redirects to home page.

rubens.notes: Orange Pippin's Rubens page is the Elstar x Gala apple but has no flavour words. NFC 'Rubens' (id 5533) is a different Dutch variety (1955, Reinette Rouge Etoilee x Cox) and was not used. Good Fruit Grower is a trade magazine; only its preview text was readable. No source mentions banana.

saturn.peak: Picked late September-early October; keeps 2-3 weeks (Orange Pippin) or until January (Walcot)
saturn.notes: No source supports our 'perfumed' tag. Storage claims differ widely.

sheeps-nose.notes: NFC has several 'Sheep's Nose' records: id 5770 (Somerset, exhibited 1883, not held) is tender, sweet, subacid; id 5772 (held since 1951) has 'hard, dry' flesh with a 'subacid' flavour. Same organisation, counted once. Not on Orange Pippin.

slack-ma-girdle.peak: In use October to December (NFC); very late, can be left on the tree or sweated before pressing (Salt Spring)
slack-ma-girdle.notes: Woody note in both Wikipedia and Salt Spring. Wikipedia cites Hogg judging it of 'not much merit' as a cider apple.

st-helens.notes: No independent page found (Orange Pippin slug redirects to home; web search found nothing).

sunrise.peak: Late August; keeps about a week refrigerated, best slightly chilled (Orange Pippin, Salt Spring)
sunrise.notes: NFC 'Sunrise (Canada)' (id 6151) is our apple; NFC 'Sunrise' (id 6150) is an unrelated English variety of 1897. No source supports our 'pear' tag; NFC alone reports strawberry.

sweet-society.peak: Picked late September, stores to December (Frank P Matthews)
sweet-society.notes: RHS plant profile (Royal Horticultural Society) recorded as 'other'. Both support 'perfumed', which our tags lack.

topaz.peak: Picked October-November; keeps 1-2 months (Orange Pippin), until March (Walcot), 4+ months refrigerated (Salt Spring)
topaz.notes: No source supports our 'berry' tag. NFC 'Topaz' (id 6374) is an unrelated English Seabrook variety; English Wikipedia's only flavour phrase cites Orange Pippin, so neither was used.

twenty-ounce.notes: Honey rests only on Orange Pippin's multi-valued style attributes. Trees of Antiquity (fetched) gives no flavour words beyond 'high quality'.

westfield-seek-no-further.peak: Picked early October / very late; stores 1-2 months (Trees of Antiquity)
westfield-seek-no-further.notes: Orange Pippin page is at slug 'seek-no-further' (westfield-seek-no-further redirects home). Nutty and honey come only from Orange Pippin's style attributes. Scott Farm notes heavy russeting in southern growing regions.

winesap.peak: Picked early to late October; stores well (3 months or more)
winesap.notes: Wine supported by Wikipedia and Trees of Antiquity; spice by Orange Pippin and Trees of Antiquity; NFC calls it only sweet-subacid.

xanthous.notes: Not found on Orange Pippin, Wikipedia or NFC.

young-america.notes: Orange Pippin slug redirects to home page; web search found no independent description.
